Small open-label studies1-3 have shown efficacy of thalidomide in patients with refractory Crohn’s disease (see under Inflammatory Bowel Disease, p.1697). In many of those patients already receiving corticoster- oids the dosage could be reduced and in some corticosteroids could be stopped completely. Reduction of TNF-α and inter- leukin-12 by thalidomide may be responsible for its clinical ef- fects in Crohn’s disease.4 Thalidomide has also been reported5 to be of benefit in children and young adults with intractable in- flammatory bowel disease (both Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis). 1.
